# Qualification-only positive no-create fence

The existing fixed-branch qualification job/profile uses this action at its new SDK source pin. The source-bound record producer profile is `blazing-keydb-parity-qualification-fenced-v1`; it does not authorize another repository, branch, group, provider or runtime. All other SDK profiles/jobs retain their existing paths.

The isolated Python3.13.9 `-I -S` bootstrap captures the eight pinned pure modules before package or site execution. JIT/native/group checks precede mint; the returned ID must have an immutable read-back ACK. Only guest-contract construction, own empty scratch creation and reader-path metadata checks are eligible for ordinary positive failure. No credentials are decrypted and no SDK create/helper/import capability is opened in that phase.

Before runtime imports, the child irreversibly enters MAY_CREATE and requests the exact live parent's volatile reservation ACK. The parent irreversibly poisons NO_CREATE before replying. This is not a durable reservation or cross-run CAS. Missing/partial/mismatched ACK cannot unlock imports. A runtime reservation, any later failure, signal, killed child, missing phase/readback, or uncertain exit never yields NO_CREATE.

On a supported pure failure, the child poisons its own state and durably acknowledges FENCE, then exits66/no signal. Only the same current parent with zero reserved create frames may upload/read back NO_CREATE. It is linked to the exact JIT ACK and producer binding. It contains no owner/DSEQ or credential material. This route is not cancellation qualification or full cleanup.

The final refinement also corrects the successful main output placement to the existing KeyDB qualification group, rather than the inherited scanner prefix. Frozen7edf remains HOLD; the actual successful entry output mapping has separate original RED and corrected positive evidence.
